title: “God Is Love”… But Not the Love You Were Told About
paragraphs:
“God Is Love”… But Not the Love You Were Told About
The dangerous misunderstanding that comforts people straight into spiritual silence—and the truth that will either break you or bring you back to life
You’ve heard it your whole life.
“God is love.”
It’s printed on mugs. Whispered at funerals. Posted under filtered sunsets. Used to excuse compromise. Used to avoid conviction. Used to silence truth.

But somewhere along the way…
we stopped asking what that actually means.
And that silence has cost more souls than we realize.

Because the world didn’t reject “God is love.”
It redefined it.
And the version it created… doesn’t save.
It numbs.
It comforts people on the edge of eternity while they slowly drift away from the very God they claim to believe in.

I remember sitting in a room full of people who said they loved God… but no one trembled at His Word anymore. No one repented. No one wept. No one wrestled. Everyone just… existed in a version of faith that felt good but required nothing.
That’s when it hit me.
We weren’t worshiping God as He revealed Himself.
We were worshiping a version of love that never existed.
Scripture doesn’t leave “God is love” open to interpretation.
It says it clearly:
“Ὁ Θεὸς ἀγάπη ἐστίν” (Ho Theos agapē estin) — 1 John 4:8
God is agapē.
Not preference. Not tolerance. Not emotional approval.
Agapē is a love that gives… but also a love that purifies.
A love that embraces… but also confronts.
A love that saves… but also demands surrender.
The Hebrew Scriptures echo this tension in a way modern ears struggle to accept:

“יְהוָה יְהוָה אֵל רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן… וְנַקֵּה לֹא יְנַקֶּה”
(YHWH, YHWH, El rachum ve’chanun… ve’nakkeh lo yenakkeh) — Exodus 34:6–7

The LORD is compassionate and gracious…
but He will by no means clear the guilty.
That doesn’t fit the version of love we were taught.
Because the world says love means acceptance without transformation.
God says love means transformation because of truth.
And that’s where most people quietly walk away.
Not loudly. Not dramatically.
Just slowly.
Because real love… the kind God embodies… exposes things we’d rather keep hidden.

It reveals pride we’ve learned to dress up as confidence.
It confronts sin we’ve learned to rename as personality.
It dismantles identities we’ve built outside of Him.

And if we’re honest…
that kind of love feels uncomfortable.
So we soften it.
We reshape it.
We turn “God is love” into something manageable.

Something that won’t interrupt our habits.
Something that won’t challenge our desires.
Something that won’t call us to die to ourselves.
But Jesus never did that.
Not once.
He looked at people with love… and then He said things that changed everything.

To the woman caught in sin:
“Neither do I condemn you… go, and sin no more.” (John 8:11)

To His disciples:
“If anyone would come after Me, let him deny himself…” (Matthew 16:24)
To the rich young ruler… He loved him… and then told him to give up everything.
That’s agapē.
Not approval.
Not comfort.
Not silence.
Sacrificial, truth-filled, soul-awakening love.

The kind that doesn’t just meet you where you are…
but refuses to leave you there.
And maybe that’s what you’ve been running from.
Not God.
But the version of Him you were never shown.
Because deep down… you know something isn’t right.

You feel it in quiet moments.
In the middle of the night.
When the noise fades and your thoughts get louder.

You know a love that never corrects…
isn’t really love.

You know a God who never confronts…
isn’t the God of Scripture.
And maybe that realization stings a little.
Or a lot.
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected, didn’t it?
Because this isn’t about shame.
It’s about awakening.

It’s about realizing that the same love that convicts you…
is the same love that was nailed to a cross for you.

“Ἀγάπη… Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν”
(Agapē… Christos apethanen hyper hēmōn) — Romans 5:8
Love… is that Christ died for us.
Not when we were perfect.
But while we were still sinners.
That’s the part people love to quote.
But they stop there.

Because if you keep reading Scripture…
that love doesn’t just forgive.
It transforms.
It calls.
It rebuilds.
It rewrites everything.
From scandal… to grace.

And if you’ve been living in a version of love that never changed you…
then maybe you’ve never truly encountered Him.
Not fully.
Not deeply.
Not yet.
But you can.
Right now.
Not by pretending you’re okay.
Not by hiding behind “God understands.”
But by surrendering.
By coming honestly.
By letting His love do what it was always meant to do.

Heal you…
and change you.
Someone you love is living in a false version of love right now.
And if you’re serious about going deeper—about not just hearing truth but living it—then stay close.
Because this isn’t about content.
It’s about transformation.
Not out of pressure… but purpose. Because reaching more souls requires obedience, not silence.

Because “God is love”…
but not the kind that leaves you unchanged.
The kind that breaks chains… and calls you by a new name.
